title: UP BOARD CLASS 2 — Environmental Studies | Plants Growth
description: Subject-wise test on Plants Growth (Environmental Studies) for UP BOARD CLASS 2. 25Q.
subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Which part of a plant usually grows under the ground?

options.explanation: Leaves grow above the ground and are responsible for photosynthesis.
Flowers grow above the ground and are involved in reproduction.
Roots grow under the ground and absorb water and nutrients.
Stems grow above the ground and support the plant.

questions.explanation: Roots are the part of the plant that typically grows downwards into the soil, anchoring the plant and absorbing water and nutrients.
questions.hint: This part helps the plant stay fixed in the soil and absorbs water.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: What do seeds need to start growing into a baby plant?

options.explanation: Soil alone is not sufficient; seeds need water, air, and warmth to germinate.
These are the essential factors for seed germination.
Sunlight is needed after germination, not during the initial sprouting phase.
Fertilizer is not required for the initial germination process.

questions.explanation: Seeds require water, air (oxygen), and a suitable temperature (warmth) to germinate and begin growing. Sunlight becomes crucial once the seedling emerges.
questions.hint: Think about the basic requirements for a seed to sprout.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Which part of the plant makes food for the whole plant using sunlight?

options.explanation: Roots absorb water and nutrients but do not make food.
Stems support the plant and transport water but do not make food.
Leaves perform photosynthesis to make food for the plant.
Flowers are involved in reproduction, not food production.

questions.explanation: Leaves contain chlorophyll and are the primary site where plants make their food through photosynthesis, using sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide.
questions.hint: This part is green and helps the plant produce food.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: What is a very young plant that has just started to grow from a seed called?

options.explanation: A tree is a mature plant, not a young one.
A bush is a larger, mature plant.
A seedling is the young plant that grows from a seed.
A flower is a part of a mature plant, not a young plant.

questions.explanation: A seedling is the stage when a seed has germinated and developed its first true leaves and root, becoming a small, young plant.
questions.hint: This is the early stage of a plant's life after germination.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: If a plant does not get enough water, what will most likely happen to it?

options.text: It will grow bigger and stronger.
options.explanation: Lack of water will not help the plant grow; it will weaken it.

options.text: It will wilt and dry up.
options.explanation: Without water, plants lose turgor pressure and wilt.
Water stress typically reduces flowering.

options.text: Its leaves will turn darker green.
options.explanation: Lack of water usually causes leaves to turn yellow or brown.

questions.explanation: Water is essential for plants to stand upright and carry out their functions. Without enough water, they lose turgor pressure, causing them to wilt and eventually die.
questions.hint: Think about the effects of dehydration on plants.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Which of these helps the plant stand upright and carries water to all its parts?

options.explanation: Roots absorb water but do not support the plant or transport water to other parts.
The stem supports the plant and transports water and nutrients.
Leaves make food but do not support the plant or transport water.
Fruits contain seeds but do not support the plant or transport water.

questions.explanation: The stem provides support for the plant, allowing it to stand upright, and also acts as a transport system, carrying water and nutrients from the roots to the leaves and other parts.
questions.hint: This part connects the roots to the leaves and supports the plant.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Which of these is NOT needed for a healthy plant to grow big and strong?

options.explanation: Sunlight is essential for photosynthesis.
Water is essential for nutrient absorption and turgor pressure.
Air provides carbon dioxide for photosynthesis.
A dark room prevents photosynthesis, which is necessary for plant growth.

questions.explanation: Plants need sunlight to make food. A dark room would prevent photosynthesis, making it impossible for a plant to grow big and strong, or even survive for long.
questions.hint: Think about the essential requirements for plant growth.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: When a flower dies, what can it sometimes turn into?

options.explanation: A flower does not turn into a leaf.
A flower does not turn into a stem.
After pollination, the flower develops into a fruit containing seeds.
A flower does not turn into roots.

questions.explanation: After pollination, the flower's ovary develops into a fruit, which contains the seeds of the plant.
questions.hint: Think about what happens to a flower after it is pollinated.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: A gardener plants a seed in a pot and gives it water every day. But he keeps the pot inside a closed, dark cupboard. What will happen to the seed?

options.text: It will grow very tall and strong because it gets water.
options.explanation: Water alone is not enough; sunlight is required for healthy growth.

options.text: It might sprout, but the plant will be pale and weak and eventually die.
options.explanation: The seed may sprout due to water, but without sunlight, the plant will not thrive.

options.text: It will not grow at all because it is dark.
options.explanation: The seed may still sprout due to water, but the plant will not grow healthily.

options.text: It will grow only roots, but no stem or leaves.
options.explanation: The seed may sprout, but the plant will be weak and pale, not just roots.

questions.explanation: A seed needs water to germinate (sprout). However, for a plant to grow healthily with green leaves, it needs sunlight to make food. Without light, it will not be able to photosynthesize and will become etiolated (pale and weak) and eventually die.
questions.hint: Consider the role of sunlight in plant growth.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Which of these statements about plant growth is *incorrect*?

options.explanation: Plants need air (carbon dioxide) for photosynthesis.

options.text: Roots help a plant to absorb water from the soil.
options.explanation: Roots absorb water and nutrients from the soil.

options.text: Fruits contain seeds that can grow into new plants.
options.explanation: Fruits contain seeds that can germinate into new plants.

options.text: Leaves absorb water for the whole plant.
options.explanation: Leaves do not absorb water; roots do.

questions.explanation: Leaves are primarily responsible for making food (photosynthesis) and releasing oxygen. Roots are the parts of the plant that absorb water and nutrients from the soil, not leaves.
questions.hint: Identify the statement that does not align with known plant biology.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Which part of a plant usually grows under the ground?

options.explanation: Leaves grow above the ground and are responsible for photosynthesis.
Flowers grow above the ground and are involved in reproduction.
Roots grow under the ground and anchor the plant while absorbing water and nutrients.
Fruits grow above the ground and contain seeds for reproduction.

questions.explanation: The root is the part of the plant that typically grows downwards into the soil, anchoring the plant and absorbing water and nutrients.
questions.hint: Think about the part of the plant that is hidden in the soil.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: What do plants need to grow big and strong, besides water and soil?

options.explanation: Stones do not help plants grow.
Toys are not a requirement for plant growth.
Sunlight is essential for photosynthesis, which helps plants produce food.
Sweets are not a natural requirement for plant growth.

questions.explanation: Plants need sunlight for photosynthesis, the process by which they make their own food to grow.
questions.hint: Think about what helps plants produce food.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: From which part does a new plant usually begin its life?

options.explanation: Flowers are part of the mature plant and are involved in reproduction.
Leaves grow from a seedling and are not the starting point.
Stems grow from a seedling and support the plant.
Seeds are the starting point of a plant's life cycle.

questions.explanation: Most plants start their life cycle as a seed, which germinates and grows into a new plant.
questions.hint: Think about the starting point of a plant's life cycle.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Which part of the plant is responsible for making food for the entire plant?

options.explanation: Leaves are the primary site for photosynthesis, where food is made.
Roots absorb water and nutrients but do not make food.
Stems support the plant but do not make food.
Flowers are involved in reproduction and do not make food.

questions.explanation: Leaves contain chlorophyll and are the primary site for photosynthesis, where plants convert sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into food.
questions.hint: Think about the part of the plant that captures sunlight.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: A small plant that has just started growing from a seed is called a:

options.explanation: A tree is a mature plant, not a small plant starting to grow.
A seedling is a young plant that has just started growing from a seed.
A shrub is a mature woody plant, not a small plant starting to grow.
A fruit is a mature part of the plant that contains seeds.

questions.explanation: A seedling is a young plant, typically germinated from a seed.
questions.hint: Think about the early stage of a plant's growth after germination.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: If you keep a plant in a completely dark room, what will most likely happen to it?

options.explanation: Plants need sunlight to grow, so they will not grow faster in the dark.

options.text: It will stop growing and may die.
options.explanation: Without sunlight, plants cannot perform photosynthesis and will eventually die.

options.text: Its leaves will turn darker green.
options.explanation: Leaves may turn yellow or pale in the dark, not darker green.

options.text: It will start producing more flowers.
options.explanation: Plants need sunlight to produce flowers, so this will not happen in the dark.

questions.explanation: Plants need sunlight to make food (photosynthesis). Without sunlight, they cannot produce food and will eventually stop growing and die.
questions.hint: Think about what happens when a plant cannot get sunlight.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Why is soil important for a growing plant?

options.text: It makes the plant smell good.
options.explanation: Soil does not affect the smell of the plant.
Soil does not help plants fly.
Soil anchors the plant and provides essential nutrients and water.

options.text: It protects the plant from rain.
options.explanation: Soil does not protect the plant from rain.

questions.explanation: Soil anchors the plant, providing stability, and contains essential nutrients and water that the roots absorb for growth.
questions.hint: Think about the role of soil in supporting and nourishing the plant.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Which of these is the correct order of a plant's growth?

options.explanation: This order is incorrect as flowers do not come before the seedling.
This order is incorrect as the plant does not come before the seed.
This is the correct order of a plant's growth.
This order is incorrect as it starts with the flower.

questions.explanation: The typical life cycle begins with a seed, which grows into a seedling, then a mature plant, which eventually produces flowers.
questions.hint: Think about the stages a plant goes through from the beginning to maturity.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: **Assertion (A):** Leaves are very important for a plant's survival. **Reason (R):** Leaves help the plant to make its own food using sunlight.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is not the correct explanation for A.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true, but R is the correct explanation for A.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation for A.
options.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.text: A is true but R is false.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

options.text: A is false but R is true.
options.explanation: Both A and R are true.

questions.explanation: The assertion that leaves are important is true. The reason provided, that leaves make food using sunlight, is also true and directly explains why leaves are crucial for survival.
questions.hint: Consider the role of leaves in the plant's survival and the reason provided.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: A small plant needs sunlight, water, and fresh air to grow. If a plant is given enough water and sunlight but kept in a closed jar with no fresh air, what will happen?

options.text: It will grow very tall and strong.
options.explanation: Without fresh air, the plant cannot perform photosynthesis properly and will not grow tall and strong.

options.text: It will produce many flowers quickly.
options.explanation: Without fresh air, the plant cannot produce flowers properly.

options.text: It will not grow well and may become weak.
options.explanation: Without fresh air, the plant cannot perform photosynthesis properly and will become weak.

options.text: It will change its colour to blue.
options.explanation: There is no natural process where a plant changes its color to blue due to lack of fresh air.

questions.explanation: Plants need fresh air (specifically carbon dioxide from the air) for photosynthesis to make food. Without fresh air, even with water and sunlight, the plant cannot grow properly and will become weak.
questions.hint: Think about the role of fresh air in the plant's growth process.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Which of these is NOT needed by a plant to grow?

options.explanation: Sunlight is essential for photosynthesis, the process by which plants make food.
Water is necessary for nutrient absorption and photosynthesis.
Air provides carbon dioxide, which is used in photosynthesis.
Stones are not a nutrient or essential element for plant growth.

questions.explanation: Plants need sunlight, water, and air to grow. Stones are not a nutrient or essential element for plant growth.
questions.hint: Think about what plants use for photosynthesis and survival.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Which part of a plant helps it to stand upright and carries water and food to all other parts?

options.explanation: Roots anchor the plant and absorb water and nutrients but do not carry them to other parts.
The stem supports the plant and transports water and food to all parts.
Flowers are primarily for reproduction and do not support the plant or transport nutrients.
Leaves make food but do not support the plant or transport water and nutrients.

questions.explanation: The stem is the main support structure of the plant that grows above the ground and transports water and nutrients from the roots to the leaves and flowers.
questions.hint: This part acts like a pipeline for the plant.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: A small seed is planted in the soil. What is the most important thing it needs to get *from the soil* to start growing into a baby plant?

options.explanation: Sunlight is important for growth but not the first thing a seed needs from the soil.
Air is needed for respiration but not the primary requirement for germination.
Water is essential for a seed to absorb and start the germination process.
Warmth aids germination but is not absorbed from the soil as a primary need.

questions.explanation: While sunlight, air, and warmth are important for overall growth, water is crucial for a seed to germinate and sprout from the soil. The seed absorbs water to begin the growth process.
questions.hint: Think about what a seed absorbs first to start growing.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: What is the main job of the leaves on a plant?

options.text: To hold the plant firmly in the soil.
options.explanation: This is the job of the roots, not the leaves.

options.text: To make food for the plant using sunlight.
options.explanation: Leaves perform photosynthesis to produce food for the plant.
Flowers attract insects for pollination, not leaves.

options.text: To help the plant drink water from the soil.
options.explanation: Roots absorb water from the soil, not leaves.

questions.explanation: Leaves are like the 'kitchen' of the plant. They use sunlight, air (carbon dioxide), and water to make food for the entire plant, a process called photosynthesis.
questions.hint: Think about what leaves produce for the plant.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs

questions.question: Rina planted a seed in a dark room and forgot to water it. Her friend, Ali, planted a similar seed outside in the garden and watered it every day. Whose seed is more likely to grow into a plant, and why?

options.text: Rina's, because seeds grow well in the dark.
options.explanation: Seeds do not grow well in the dark; they need light for photosynthesis.

options.text: Ali's, because it received both sunlight and water.
options.explanation: Ali's seed had the necessary sunlight and water for growth.

options.text: Rina's, because indoor plants always grow faster.
options.explanation: Indoor plants do not necessarily grow faster; they often lack proper light.

options.text: Ali's, because seeds need to be forgotten to grow.
options.explanation: Seeds do not need to be forgotten to grow; they need proper care and conditions.

questions.explanation: Plants need both sunlight and water to grow. Ali's seed got the necessary sunlight from being outside and water from being watered daily, making it much more likely to grow compared to Rina's seed which lacked both.
questions.hint: Consider the essential requirements for plant growth.
questions.subject: upbo2-evs
